passages.source_title: OWASP SQL Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet
passages.text: SQL injection risk arises when data is combined with SQL command syntax. Use prepared statements and bound parameters to keep values separate from the SQL structure; assess whether inputs are externally influenced.

passages.source_title: OWASP SQL Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet
passages.text: When SQL identifiers cannot be bound as parameters, validate them against a strict allowlist. Input validation can provide defense in depth but is not a substitute for parameterizing SQL values.

Improper handling of special elements in SQL commands can permit unintended modification of a query. A dynamic query is an indicator requiring investigation, not by itself proof of an exploitable vulnerability.

With Python subprocess calls, an argument list and shell=False usually avoid routing a command through a shell. When shell=True is needed, assess shell quoting and whether command parts can come from untrusted input.
OS command injection may arise when external input influences shell command construction. Verify the input source, dataflow, and execution context before concluding exploitation is possible.
